subject: Supplier sunset schedule and hosting fallback plan
messages:
From: Michael Chu <michael.chu@fintechcorp.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fintechcorp.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: detailed supplier exit & fallback plan for Redwood services

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the quick call earlier. As part of our production intake and vendor risk review, our security and procurement teams need a short written plan that covers: 1) any suppliers/subprocessors that are planned for deprecation in the next 12 months, 2) the fallback or migration path if a primary cloud region or partner is deprecated, and 3) how customer data is exported/handed off during transitions.

Can you provide a roster of impacted vendors plus a short hosting fallback playbook for US regions (we run critical services in us-west-2)? Ideally something we can attach to the contract as an operational appendix.

Best,
Michael
Michael Chu
Head of Procurement, FinTechCorp

--
Attachment: FT-MC-RFP-questions.pdf (application/pdf, 98KB)

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example.com>
To: Michael Chu <michael.chu@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: detailed supplier exit & fallback plan for Redwood services

Hi Michael — thanks, sending an initial package below and attaching the vendor roster and a hosting fallback playbook for us-west-2. Key points up front:

- No planned deprecations of first-line subprocessors in the next 12 months except for one legacy logging vendor slated for Q4 that we will replace with an in-house pipeline.
- We maintain active multi-region fallbacks for model serving; primary is us-west-2, fallback is us-east-1 with automated KV and prefix cache replication.
- Data export during migrations uses customer-scoped export bundles (encrypted, integrity-checked, delivered via secure transfer to customer S3 or via customer SFTP).

Im also including a proposed operational appendix (see attachment). If you want, I can schedule a short follow-up with our infra lead Karthik to go into replication and playbook details.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood_vendor_roster_q2_2027.pdf (PDF, 240KB); fallback-playbook-AWS-us-west-2.docx (DOCX, 56KB)

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: vendor sunset Q4 logging vendor — migration checklist

Folks,

Putting a brief checklist here so we have a coordinated message to FinTechCorp:

- Confirm contract termination dates with legacy-logger (current expiry 2027-10-31). Need legal to clear early termination penalties. (Action: Rishi)
- Draft migration timeline for customers on legacy-logger: export windows, retention implications, verification steps. (Action: Karthik)
- Update our host-fallback playbook to call out how KV cache will warm in us-east-1 and estimated cold-start latency. Include rollback steps. (Action: Karthik + Infra)
- Prepare a signed subprocessor notice for customers impacted by the logging change; include contact for data export/requests. (Action: Olga)

Also note: Marissa — please confirm if any enterprise customers have custom retention rules that would require special handling during the export.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Product Ops

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example.com>
To: Michael Chu <michael.chu@fintechcorp.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Supplier sunset notice & hosting fallback appendix (FT-4521)

Michael — attaching the finalized materials for your vendor risk pack. Highlights below for the appendix: 

1) Subprocessor sunset: legacy-logger (supplier id: LEG-113) — planned migration window 2027-10-01 to 2027-10-31. Customers will receive export bundles containing logs for the retention period specified in their contract. We will support export delivery to a customer-managed S3 bucket or SFTP endpoint; encrypted with AES-256 and signed with SHA-256.

2) Hosting fallback (us-west-2 -> us-east-1): automated route: R1 -> R2 with DNS TTL 60s, KV prefix replication every 5 minutes, cache warm-up policy that prefetches last 1 hour of active keys. Expected cold-start token latency increase during failover: +120-250ms for first 30 minutes while caches warm.

3) Data handoff & evidence: all transfer logs, md5 checksums, and transfer manifests will be provided as part of the export bundle. We will also include a signed subprocessor notice (attached) and a rollback decision tree.

Attached: redwood_vendor_roster_q2_2027.pdf; fallback-playbook-AWS-us-west-2.docx; subprocessor-notice-FT-4521-signed.pdf

If you want a quick walk-through, I can loop Karthik and Rishi into a 30-minute call. Let me know which day works this week.

Best,
Olga
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
